title: The Post Office to the Acid Barrel: the Ten Weeks of the Congo and the Tooth Returned
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Sankuru and the Post Office

stops.name: Onalua, the birth in Tetela country
stops.date_confidence: date attested; the pin is the Katako-Kombe territorial centre, since no source in the pool fixes the village, and it corrects a gathering coordinate that fell near Mbuji-Mayi, 300 km south
stops.campa: A son is born to a Tetela farming family at Onalua, in the Katako-Kombe country, where the colony keeps cotton quotas and mission registers and very little else. They name him Isaïe Tasumbu Tawosa; the Patrice Émery comes later, at a school desk. The nearest railhead is days away and the nearest river port further. The birth is written down at all only because a mission catechist keeps a book. A century on, the administration will carve this ground out of its territory and call the new city Lumumbaville.
suggested_refs: The Katako-Kombe country of the Sankuru, Tetela territory, birthplace region of Patrice Lumumba

stops.name: Sankuru mission belt, the double schooling
stops.date_confidence: decade only; the station is not named in any source consulted, and the order of the Protestant and Catholic schooling differs between the English and French accounts
stops.campa: The boy passes through a Protestant primary school and a Catholic mission school, the ordinary double track of a colonial child whose family does not choose which church owns the nearest classroom, and then through a government post office training school. He comes out carrying Tetela, French, Lingala, Swahili and Tshiluba, five languages for a country that does not yet exist. Which station taught him what, no reachable source says. The mission classroom is the first colonial machine he learns to work from the inside.
suggested_refs: A Congolese mission-school classroom of the 1930s, Sankuru region

stops.name: Stanleyville, eleven years at the post office
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the move; the eleven years run to 1956
stops.campa: He arrives on the great bend of the river as a postal clerk, after a season selling beer town to town for a brewery in Léopoldville. Eleven years pass at the counter. He marries Henriette Maletaua, divorces, marries Hortense Sombosia, divorces, and in 1951 marries Pauline Opango, who is fourteen and who will be his widow ten years later. The post office gives him a salary and a fixed address. It also gives him correspondents in every district of the colony. It is the least revolutionary job available in the Congo and it builds him a list of names.
suggested_refs: The colonial post office at Stanleyville on the bend of the Congo River

stops.name: Stanleyville, the évolué associations
stops.date_confidence: ADAPÉS and the Clément post attested to 1952; the Cercles headship and the Liberal Party card to 1955
stops.campa: Hired as personal assistant to the French sociologist Pierre Clément, he co-founds the ADAPÉS alumni association and begins the associational climb that the colony has designed as a substitute for politics. By 1955 he heads the regional Cercles network and holds a card in the Liberal Party of Belgium, a colonial subject enrolled in the metropole's own party. The clubs are meant to produce well-mannered évolués. They produce a man with a mailing list and a printing habit, read in every provincial capital of the Congo.
suggested_refs: An évolué association meeting in a Congolese provincial capital, 1950s

stops.name: Stanleyville, the embezzlement conviction
stops.date_confidence: arrest 1956 and conviction 1957 attested; the twelve-month sentence is attested, the months are not
stops.campa: He writes an autobiography, travels to Belgium on a study tour, and comes home to a warrant over postal funds. The court gives him twelve months and a fine. Belgian accounts read a clerk living beyond his salary; Congolese accounts read a colonial state making an example of a man already too visible in the clubs. The atlas records both and settles neither. He goes into the cell as an association secretary and comes out in 1957 with nothing left to lose in the career the mission schools had drawn for him.
suggested_refs: The colonial prison at Stanleyville, where Lumumba served the 1957 sentence
sources: Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Léopoldville, the Brasserie de Léo
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month inferred
stops.campa: Out of prison, he takes the capital and a job as sales director for the Brasserie de Léo et du Bas-Congo, selling beer up and down the river towns he will be campaigning in within a year. The post carries a car, an expense account, and a reason to be in every quarter of Léopoldville. He reads the capital's newspapers and stands close enough to the colonial administration to take its measure. The brewery office is the last salaried desk of his life, and he keeps it for about a year.
suggested_refs: The Brasserie de Léo et du Bas-Congo, Léopoldville, where Lumumba was sales director in 1957-1958

stops.name: Léopoldville, the founding of the MNC
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the fifth of October he and a small circle found the Mouvement National Congolais, the first Congolese party organized on the country rather than on a people. It is a deliberate wager against the ethnic federations already forming in Kasaï and the Bas-Congo: one Congo, one movement, and his name attached to both. Belgium has spent eighty years teaching that the Congo is a collection of tribes held together by Brussels. The MNC answers that the Congo is one country, and it carries him to the premiership in under two years.
suggested_refs: The founding circle of the Mouvement National Congolais, Léopoldville, October 1958

stops.name: Accra, the All-African Peoples' Conference
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day inferred
stops.campa: He crosses to Ghana for the All-African Peoples' Conference and meets Kwame Nkrumah in a hall where pan-Africanism is spoken as policy rather than as sentiment. Independence is discussed there as a date, not as an eventual reward for good conduct. He goes home and stops asking for reform. The Belgian administration begins to file him under a different heading: no longer an évolué with grievances, now an organizer with foreign friends and a printing press.
suggested_refs: The All-African Peoples' Conference, Accra, December 1958, with Nkrumah presiding

stops.name: Stanleyville, the riot, the arrest, the sentence
stops.date_confidence: riot and arrest October 1959, day not fixed; French Wikipedia gives sentencing 21 January 1960 and release 26 January, against a gathering-pass claim of an 18 January trial opening that no consulted source supports
stops.campa: An MNC congress in Stanleyville ends in a riot in which about thirty people are killed, and the administration arrests him for inciting it. He is still in the cell when Belgium convenes the conference that will negotiate the handover of the Congo. Six months are pronounced against him in January; within days the Congolese delegates in Brussels refuse to continue without him, and the sentence dissolves. The colony has arranged to give away a country and to imprison the man it must give it to, inside the same fortnight.
suggested_refs: The Stanleyville courthouse, January 1960, where Lumumba was sentenced days before his release

stops.name: Brussels, the Round Table and the thirtieth of June
stops.date_confidence: release 26 January per French Wikipedia; the conference had opened on 20 January and fixed the independence date on 27 January
stops.campa: He goes from a Stanleyville prison into a Brussels conference hall inside the same week, and some Belgian officials at the table learn of the change in his status when he walks in. On the twenty-seventh the conference fixes independence for the thirtieth of June, a date chosen for Belgian convenience and not for any administrative readiness in the Congo. There are five months in which to build a state. He leaves Brussels a prime minister in waiting, having spent the previous month as a convict of the government across the table.
suggested_refs: The Congolese Round Table Conference, Brussels, January-February 1960

stops.name: Léopoldville, the elections and the investiture
stops.date_confidence: attested; corrects a gathering claim that he became prime minister at the 30 June ceremony, when the premiership runs from 24 June
stops.campa: The MNC takes a plurality in the first national elections in May. On the twenty-first of June he is named formateur; on the twenty-third his thirty-seven-member government is formed and approved by the Chamber seventy-four to five that night and by the Senate sixty to twelve before dawn. He is prime minister on the twenty-fourth, six days before the country exists. The republic is assembled in seventy-two hours by men whom the colony never permitted to hold an administrative post above clerk.
suggested_refs: The Lumumba Government of 23 June 1960, thirty-seven ministers

stops.name: Palais de la Nation, the speech before the king
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate follows French Wikipedia and corrects a gathering pin about 5 km southeast of the building
stops.campa: King Baudouin has praised the genius of Leopold II, and Kasa-Vubu has thanked him for it. Lumumba then rises, unscheduled, and reads the colony back to itself: forced labour paid at wages that fed no one, the mansions for the whites and the huts for the blacks, a law lenient to one colour and cruel to the other, the black man addressed as tu because vous was reserved for the white. The court expects gratitude and receives an indictment, delivered in the king's hearing and in his own language.
stops.quote: Morning, noon and night we were subjected to jeers, insults and blows because we were 'Negroes'.
stops.quote_source: Patrice Lumumba, Independence Day speech, Léopoldville, 30 June 1960; English translation, Lumumba Internet Archive (marxists.org)
suggested_refs: The independence ceremony at the Palais de la Nation, 30 June 1960, Baudouin seated on the dais

stops.name: Palais de la Nation, what the speech promised
stops.date_confidence: attested; same ceremony, later in the same address
stops.campa: The indictment is only the first half. The second half is a set of undertakings: to make the Congo the pride of Africa, to show what free labour can do, to treat this independence as a step toward the liberation of the whole continent. He is speaking as the head of a government six days old, in a country with a handful of university graduates and an officer corps entirely Belgian. Within ten weeks every promise in the second half will be in the hands of other governments.
stops.quote: The Congo's independence is a decisive step towards the liberation of the whole African continent.
stops.quote_source: Patrice Lumumba, Independence Day speech, Léopoldville, 30 June 1960; Lumumba Internet Archive (marxists.org)
suggested_refs: The printed text of the Independence Day speech, 30 June 1960

stops.name: Léopoldville, the mutiny and the Armée Nationale Congolaise
stops.date_confidence: attested; mutiny from 5 July, Janssens dismissed 6 July, renaming and appointments 8 July
stops.campa: Five days after independence the Force Publique mutinies against an officer corps that is still entirely Belgian. On the sixth he dismisses its commander, General Émile Janssens, who had written on a blackboard that after independence equals before independence. On the eighth the force becomes the Armée Nationale Congolaise, Victor Lundula is made general and Joseph Mobutu chief of staff. An army is Africanized in seventy-two hours by a government eight days old, and the chief of staff appointed that week is the man who will take him.
suggested_refs: The Force Publique mutiny of July 1960 and the creation of the Armée Nationale Congolaise

stops.name: Élisabethville, the secession of Katanga
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Belgian landings 10 July, the break with Belgium and the cable to Khrushchev 14 July
stops.campa: Belgium lands roughly six thousand troops without asking the government, and on the eleventh Moïse Tshombe declares Katanga independent, taking the copper, the cobalt and Union Minière with him. Three days later Lumumba breaks relations with Brussels and cables Nikita Khrushchev for support, which converts a colonial withdrawal into a Cold War file in Washington and Moscow on the same afternoon. The province that pays for the country has left the country, eleven days after the country began.
suggested_refs: Moïse Tshombe's declaration of Katangan secession, 11 July 1960
The Union Minière du Haut-Katanga concession

stops.name: New York, the United Nations
stops.date_confidence: attested; meetings with Hammarskjöld 24-26 July
stops.campa: Five weeks into independence he comes to the United Nations to ask for force against what he calls colonial war resumed by other means. Dag Hammarskjöld gives him peacekeepers and withholds the mandate he actually wants, which is help retaking Katanga. He leaves with peacekeepers and without the mandate. The force voted for his country answers to New York and not to Léopoldville. Four years later Che Guevara will stand in this same hall and indict imperialism from the Congo to Vietnam.
suggested_refs: Lumumba at United Nations headquarters, New York, July 1960, with Secretary-General Hammarskjöld

stops.name: Washington, the State Department
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He meets Secretary of State Christian Herter and asks the United States for direct backing against the secession. The meeting is courteous and produces nothing. Brussels has already begun discussing how to be rid of him, and within weeks Eisenhower will authorize an operation to kill him, after Allen Dulles calls his removal an urgent and prime objective. He walks out of the State Department believing he has failed to persuade a possible ally. He has just paid a call on the government that will order his death.
suggested_refs: Lumumba in Washington, 27 July 1960, meeting Secretary of State Christian Herter
sources: Wikipedia, 'Assassination of Patrice Lumumba' (Church Committee findings)

stops.name: Léopoldville, the interview with TASS
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The day after Washington he gives an interview to the Soviet news agency and says on the record that the Soviet Union is the only Great Power whose stand has matched his people's will. It is the sentence the Léopoldville station has been waiting for. He is not a communist and his party is a coalition of clerks and schoolteachers, but the file does not require him to be one; it requires him to have said this in print. From this week the cables about him stop being about the Congo and become cables about Moscow.
stops.quote: There has never been a Katanga problem as such. The gist of the matter is that the imperialists want to lay their hands on our country's riches.
stops.quote_source: Patrice Lumumba, interview with TASS, 28 July 1960; Lumumba Internet Archive (marxists.org)
suggested_refs: The TASS interview of 28 July 1960 as printed in the Soviet press

stops.name: Conakry, Sékou Touré
stops.date_confidence: the tour runs 2-8 August 1960; the day of each capital is inferred
stops.campa: In Conakry he meets Sékou Touré, who broke with France so completely that the departing administration is said to have pulled out the telephones. Guinea gives the most concrete solidarity of the whole circuit, sending aircraft and material to Léopoldville later in the year. The radical African capitals send warm words and some equipment; Brussels and Washington send arithmetic. Neither column can move a copper mine back under his government's control.
suggested_refs: Lumumba's African tour of August 1960: Tunis, Rabat, Conakry, Accra, Monrovia, Lomé

stops.name: Accra, the unsigned union with Nkrumah
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day inferred; the pool's own lenses disagree over whether the agreement was signed, and the journey does not adjudicate
stops.campa: He returns to the hall where his politics changed and talks with Nkrumah about a union of their two states, one pan-African country made of Ghana and the Congo. Nothing is ratified. The conversation alone alarms other African leaders and hands his rivals at home a usable line: that he will trade Congolese sovereignty to a foreign patron, even a black African one. He flies from Lomé back to a capital where his coalition is already coming apart, having gathered communiqués, photographs, and one aircraft.
suggested_refs: Lumumba and Kwame Nkrumah, Accra, August 1960

stops.name: Bakwanga, the army in South Kasai
stops.date_confidence: attested for the arrival at Bakwanga; the secession did not end until 5 October 1962, correcting a gathering claim of 1961
stops.campa: He proclaims a state of emergency on the ninth and a special military regime on the sixteenth, then sends the army into South Kasai to end a second secession. The troops reach Bakwanga on the twenty-seventh and the operation collapses into the killing of Luba civilians, roughly three thousand of them, before the army withdraws in September. It is the act his defenders have never explained away and his enemies have never needed to exaggerate. The secession itself outlives him by more than a year and a half.
suggested_refs: The ANC offensive into South Kasai, August 1960, and the Luba civilian deaths at Bakwanga

stops.name: Léopoldville, the vials from Sidney Gottlieb
stops.date_confidence: September 1960; the day is not given in any source consulted
stops.campa: A CIA chemist named Sidney Gottlieb arrives with vials of botulinum toxin and instructions for the station chief, Larry Devlin, to get them into Lumumba's food or onto his toothbrush. Devlin does not do it. In November another officer, Michael Mulroney, refuses the same assignment and argues instead for delivering the man into hostile hands. The method Mulroney proposes is the one finally used. Nobody in Léopoldville has to poison him if Katanga can be handed the body alive and made to do the rest.
suggested_refs: The CIA poison plot of September 1960, as documented by the Church Committee

stops.name: Léopoldville, two dismissals by radio
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Chamber annulled both dismissals 60-19 on 7 September and the Senate gave confidence 49-0 with 7 abstentions on 8 September
stops.campa: President Kasa-Vubu goes on the radio and dismisses his prime minister; within hours the prime minister goes on the radio and dismisses his president. Two heads of the same state depose each other in one evening on the same transmitter, and neither dismissal carries force beyond the broadcast. On the seventh the Chamber annuls both by sixty votes to nineteen; on the eighth the Senate gives the government forty-nine to nothing with seven abstentions. Parliament has spoken, and six days later the man who holds the army settles it.
suggested_refs: The constitutional deadlock of September 1960 between Kasa-Vubu and Lumumba

stops.name: Camp Léopold II, the peaceful revolution
stops.date_confidence: the coup is attested; that Lumumba went to the camp that evening seeking Mobutu appears in one lens of the pool only and is carried as tradition
stops.campa: The colonel he promoted in July announces on the radio that he is neutralizing the president, the prime minister and parliament together, and calls it a peaceful revolution. Tradition puts Lumumba at the camp gates that same evening, looking for the officer he made. Ten weeks earlier he Africanized this army in three days. It is now the instrument that ends the republic, in the hands of the man he chose for the job and a station that has stopped writing memoranda about poison.
suggested_refs: Camp Léopold II, Léopoldville, headquarters of the Armée Nationale Congolaise in 1960

stops.name: Kalina, the residence between two cordons
stops.date_confidence: the confinement runs from late September to 27 November 1960; the pin date is nominal
stops.campa: He lives in the prime minister's residence at Kalina inside two rings of soldiers: United Nations troops outside, there to keep the army and the mob off him, and Mobutu's men beyond them, there to keep him in. Parliament still calls him prime minister. He receives visitors, dictates statements, and governs nothing at all. On the twenty-fourth of November the General Assembly in New York seats Mobutu's delegates in the chairs of his government, which ends its recognition abroad.
suggested_refs: The prime minister's residence in the Kalina district under UN and Congolese guard, autumn 1960
sources: Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Brussels, the cable of definitive elimination
stops.date_confidence: October 1960; the day is not fixed in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The Belgian minister for African affairs, Harold d'Aspremont Lynden, cables Africa calling for the definitive elimination of Lumumba. The phrase sits in a government file, in a minister's own instruction, four months after the same government handed over the country at a ceremony where the man now to be eliminated had embarrassed a king in front of his court. Forty years later a parliamentary commission in this city will read that cable back into the record and call it moral responsibility.
suggested_refs: The d'Aspremont Lynden cable of October 1960, Belgian ministry for African affairs

stops.name: Léopoldville, the escape from Kalina
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the night of the twenty-seventh, in rain, he goes through both cordons and out of the capital in a small convoy with Pauline, their young son, and a few allies. The destination is Stanleyville, a thousand kilometres east, where Antoine Gizenga holds the province in his name and where his own public life began at a post office counter. Behind him the capital belongs to the army he renamed in July. He has a head start of hours and a road that is mostly mud.
suggested_refs: The route east from Léopoldville toward Stanleyville, late November 1960

stops.name: Mweka, the roadside speech
stops.date_confidence: tradition, from De Witte at second hand; neither the stop nor its effect on the capture is settled in the sources consulted
stops.campa: Tradition holds that he stops at Mweka and gets down to speak, because he will not pass through Congolese towns without addressing the people standing in them, and that this delay is what closes the distance behind him. The soldiers are three days out of Léopoldville and gaining. No source consulted can say what the crowd actually cost him. The atlas keeps the story where it found it, as tradition, and names Ludo De Witte, cited at second hand, as its only source.
suggested_refs: Mweka, Kasaï, a road stop on Lumumba's flight east
sources: Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Lodi, the crossing of the Sankuru
stops.date_confidence: capture attested on 1 December; the crossing has no fixed coordinate in the sources consulted and this pin is an estimate on the river
stops.campa: At the river near Lodi the convoy tries to ferry across, a few hundred metres from the bank where his own province begins. Mobutu's soldiers reach them at the water. Ghanaian peacekeepers are stationed near enough to watch and do not intervene, having no mandate that covers it. Pauline and the boy are taken with him, and by most accounts it is their capture and not his that ends his resistance. He gives himself up on the wrong side of a river he was minutes from crossing.
suggested_refs: The Sankuru River crossing near Lodi, 1 December 1960

stops.name: Ndjili, the return under guard
stops.date_confidence: attested; held briefly at Port-Francqui the same day
stops.campa: He is held briefly at Port-Francqui, the river port, and flown back into the capital the same day with his hands bound, then beaten by soldiers on the ground while photographers work. The pictures travel the world within days and turn an arrest into a diplomatic crisis that Mobutu's government cannot contain even while it holds him. Five months earlier this city heard him tell a king what the colony had been. It now keeps him only long enough to settle where he should be sent to die.
suggested_refs: Photographs of Lumumba bound and beaten on his return to Léopoldville, 2 December 1960

stops.name: Camp Hardy, the letter to Dayal
stops.date_confidence: attested; the quotation is printed here with an explicit ellipsis, because the passages it joins are not contiguous in the source
stops.campa: A hundred and fifty kilometres from Léopoldville, in the military prison of Camp Hardy at Thysville, he is kept on deliberately poor rations. On the fourth of January he writes to the United Nations Special Representative, A. M. Dayal, and what he writes is an inventory rather than an appeal: the damp cell, the two bad meals, the requests for fruit and for an evening walk refused, the shirt unwashed for thirty-five days, the shoes taken away. It is a head of government writing to the organization whose troops had guarded his door.
stops.quote: We have been locked up in damp cells since December 2, 1960 and at no time have we been permitted to leave them. ... The clothes that I wear have not been washed for thirty-five days. I am forbidden to wear shoes.
stops.quote_source: Patrice Lumumba, letter to A. M. Dayal, UN Special Representative, 4 January 1961; Lumumba Internet Archive (marxists.org). The ellipsis marks omitted passages on the food and on the refused requests.
suggested_refs: Camp Hardy, Thysville (Mbanza-Ngungu), the military prison of December 1960 and January 1961

stops.name: Camp Hardy, the last letter and the mutiny of the guards
stops.date_confidence: the loss of discipline among the guards is dated 13 January; the letter to Pauline is undated in the archive and is placed here for sequence only
stops.campa: He writes to Pauline from the prison the letter that will circulate after his death as his last, telling her not to weep for him and telling the future where its historians will be trained. In the same days discipline among the guards at Camp Hardy fails, the prisoners are briefly loose inside the walls, and the alarm reaches Léopoldville and Élisabethville together. Congolese and Belgian officials agree he must be moved somewhere more secure, and choose Katanga, whose government he has spent six months trying to end.
stops.quote: The day will come when history will speak. But it will not be the history which will be taught in Brussels, Paris, Washington or the United Nations. It will be the history which will be taught in the countries which have won freedom from colonialism and its puppets.
stops.quote_source: Patrice Lumumba, letter from Thysville prison to Pauline Lumumba, 1961, undated in the archive; Lumumba Internet Archive (marxists.org)
suggested_refs: The Thysville letter to Pauline Lumumba, circulated after his death as his last letter

stops.name: Luano, the landing at Élisabethville
stops.date_confidence: attested; landing in the late afternoon
stops.campa: A DC-4 carrying Lumumba, Maurice Mpolo and Joseph Okito lands at Luano in the late afternoon, having flown west to the coast and then east across the whole country rather than a straight line. The three have been beaten in the air. Katangan soldiers beat them again on the tarmac in front of the officials waiting to receive them. The secession's chief enemy has been handed to the secession by his own country's army, with Belgian officers at both ends of the flight.
suggested_refs: Luano airport, Élisabethville, 17 January 1961, the transfer of Lumumba, Mpolo and Okito

stops.name: Brouwez farmhouse, the requisitioned evening
stops.date_confidence: attested for the evening of 17 January; the coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: The Katangan gendarmerie takes over the house of a farmer named Lucien Brouwez outside the city and holds the three men there through the evening. Belgian officers and Katangan ministers come and go, Godefroid Munongo among them, and the decision is taken inside. There is no charge, no court, no sentence and no record of a vote. A farmhouse is requisitioned for an evening because the state that wants him dead has no procedure that would produce the outcome and no intention of inventing one.
suggested_refs: The Brouwez house outside Élisabethville, where the three prisoners were held on 17 January 1961

stops.name: Shilatembo, the road toward Mwadingusha
stops.date_confidence: attested for the night of 17 January; this pin corrects an afterlife-lens coordinate that fell on Lubumbashi itself, some 50 km away
stops.campa: On a dirt road near Shilatembo, three pits have been dug. The Belgian officer Julien Gat orders three firing squads, and the men are shot one after another, each made to face his own squad apart from the others. Witnesses say Lumumba says nothing at all. A Belgian police commissioner writes four words in his private datebook: 9:43 L Dead. There is no Congolese court in this, no public record and no marker, and within a day the men who put the bodies in the ground beside the road decide the grave itself is a risk.
suggested_refs: The execution site near Shilatembo on the Mwadingusha road, 17 January 1961
The commissioner's datebook entry recording the time of death
sources: Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Kasenga, toward the Rhodesian border
stops.date_confidence: attested for the first exhumation and the move
stops.campa: The bodies are dug up and carried east toward Kasenga on the Northern Rhodesian border, as far from Élisabethville as the province allows, because a findable grave is a shrine. The line they run for is the border Cecil Rhodes's chartered company drew across this plateau seventy years earlier, when a board in London was granted a country to extract; the copper that pays for the secession lies along the same seam. Three days of driving buy them nothing. Munongo orders a second exhumation.
suggested_refs: Kasenga on the Northern Rhodesian border, where the bodies were moved on 18 January 1961

stops.name: The bush outside Élisabethville, the acid barrels
stops.date_confidence: attested for 21 January and the two days following; the clearing has no fixed coordinate and this pin is an estimate
stops.campa: On Munongo's order the bodies are raised a second time, sawn apart and dissolved in barrels of sulfuric acid supplied by Union Minière du Haut-Katanga. The Belgian police officer Gerard Soete and his brother Michel do the work across two days. By Soete's own later account almost nothing survives the barrels, and what does survive he keeps: teeth, a bullet, pieces of bone, taken home as souvenirs. A mining company's chemicals are used to ensure that the prime minister of the Congo has no body and no grave.
suggested_refs: Union Minière du Haut-Katanga, supplier of the sulfuric acid used on 21-22 January 1961

stops.name: Élisabethville, Munongo announces the death
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Twenty-seven days after the killing, Munongo tells the press that the three escaped custody and were killed by villagers in a hostile district, and declines to name the village. Riots follow in a dozen capitals. Four years on, Fidel Castro will send Che Guevara and a column of Cuban volunteers across Lake Tanganyika to fight beside the men the atlas calls the heirs of murdered Lumumba, holding the eastern mountains. The same Mobutu breaks that rebellion in 1965 and then rules the country for thirty-two years.
suggested_refs: Munongo's press conference of 13 February 1961 and the international protests that followed

stops.name: Moscow, the university takes the name
stops.date_confidence: attested; founded 5 February 1960 without his name, named 22 February 1961, name removed 5 February 1992, restored March 2023
stops.campa: Five weeks after the killing, the Peoples' Friendship University founded in Moscow the year before, to train students from the colonized and the newly free, is renamed Patrice Lumumba University. Students from thirty countries take their degrees under the name of a man killed in part for a cable he sent to the Kremlin in July 1960. In February 1992 the name is taken off the building, and stays off for thirty-one years. In March 2023 Moscow puts it back.
suggested_refs: Patrice Lumumba Peoples' Friendship University, 6 Miklukho-Maklaya Street, Moscow

stops.name: Kinshasa, Mobutu makes him a national hero
stops.date_confidence: 1966 for the consecration and the renaming of the former Boulevard Léopold II; the statue's erection date and sculptor are not established, and French Wikipedia dates a monument installation at this square to 17 January 2002
stops.campa: Five years after handing him to Katanga, Mobutu proclaims Lumumba a national hero, gives his name to the former Boulevard Léopold II, and puts a statue at its head. The man who took the country from him now needs his face on it. Authenticity follows: Congolese names for Congolese places, Zaire for Congo, and a martyr in bronze at a road junction to certify the authority of the man who made the martyr. No source consulted fixes when the statue actually went up, or whose hands made it.
suggested_refs: The Lumumba statue at the Limete interchange, Boulevard Lumumba, Kinshasa

stops.name: Washington, the Church Committee
stops.date_confidence: 1975; the day is not given in the sources consulted
stops.campa: A Senate committee under Frank Church opens the files and confirms that the CIA conspired to assassinate Lumumba, that Eisenhower authorized it, that Gottlieb's vials were real. It also finds no American hand on the trigger, which belonged to Belgians and Katangans. Two years before the report, the same machinery had put Augusto Pinochet into the Moneda over Salvador Allende's body. The committee names the design without naming the pattern; the atlas notes the pattern and marks it as its own reading, not the committee's.
suggested_refs: The Church Committee interim report on alleged assassination plots involving foreign leaders, 1975

stops.name: Sint-Kruis, what Soete kept
stops.date_confidence: Soete lived at Sint-Kruis near Bruges from 1972 until his death on 9 June 2000; 1999 attaches to De Witte's book, and the claim of a televised display is unverified, correcting a gathering location in Uccle some 250 km away
stops.campa: For nearly forty years a retired Belgian police officer keeps in a house outside Bruges the teeth he took from a dissolved body, and a bullet, while his government denies any part in the death. Then he talks: to Ludo De Witte for a book, and by some accounts on camera. Sources disagree over whether it was one tooth or two incisors, over the finger bones, over the broadcast. What no source disputes is that the only physical remnant of Patrice Lumumba spent the end of the century in a drawer in Flanders.
suggested_refs: Gerard Soete's house at Sint-Kruis, Bruges, where the relics were kept until 2016
sources: Ludo De Witte, De Moord op Patrice Lumumba (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Brussels, the inquiry and the apology
stops.date_confidence: the commission reported in 2001 and the apology followed in 2002; the day of the apology is not given in the sources consulted
stops.campa: A parliamentary commission spends two years in the files that d'Aspremont Lynden's cable sits in, and concludes that Belgium bears moral responsibility for the circumstances of the death. The government apologizes to the Congolese people. It is forty-one years since the barrels, and the surviving participants are old men in Flemish towns. No one is prosecuted. The state that ordered a definitive elimination admits, in the careful language of a committee, that it did not want him alive.
suggested_refs: The Belgian parliamentary commission of inquiry into the assassination of Lumumba, 2000-2001

stops.name: Egmont Palace, the tooth handed over
stops.date_confidence: attested; the court order that made it possible is dated 10 September 2020
stops.campa: A Belgian court has ordered the surviving tooth taken from the Soete family and given to the family it was taken from. At the Egmont Palace, before his children, the prime minister Alexander De Croo apologizes and a small box is carried across a room. The Belgian state, which took a whole man and returns one tooth, performs the return with full protocol, an honour guard and a flag. Sixty-one years of official denial end in an afternoon's ceremony, around an object that fits in the palm of a hand.
suggested_refs: The handover ceremony at Egmont Palace, Brussels, 20 June 2022
sources: Reuters and AP coverage of the 2022 repatriation

stops.name: Limete, the mausoleum at the Place de la Reconstruction
stops.date_confidence: attested; the mausoleum stands in Limete per French Wikipedia, correcting a gathering pin in central Gombe about 8 km away
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of June, sixty-two years to the day after he told a king what the colony had been, the tooth is interred in a new mausoleum at the Place de la Reconstruction, beside the interchange where Mobutu's statue of him stands. Three days of national mourning are decreed. In November 2024 the mausoleum is vandalized and the tooth is reported secure. The republic gives him a grave with his name on it, built around one tooth and a great deal of argument that has not finished.
suggested_refs: The Lumumba mausoleum at the Place de la Reconstruction, Limete, Kinshasa, inaugurated 30 June 2022
